sources.title: E. Hairer and G. Wanner, Solving Ordinary Differential Equations II, Chapter VI: Iterative Methods—Nonlinear Equations
sources.locator: Complete 14-page chapter PDF fetched and inspected. Complete relevant sections: §VI.1, printed pp. 134–136 / PDF pp. 1–2; §VI.3, printed pp. 138–141 / PDF pp. 5–7.

contents.name: §VI.1 fixed-point reformulation, iteration, and residual stopping discussion
contents.reason: Supports the iteration interface and distinction between residual stopping and a proved convergence bound; the local algorithm explicitly adds finite-budget statuses.

contents.name: §VI.3 Newton linearization and system update (3.1)–(3.4)
contents.reason: Supports the exact-Jacobian correction equation; statuses, residual-only stopping order, and finite budget are stated locally.

contents.name: §VI.3 numerical Jacobian formula (3.8), truncation expansion (3.9), and roundoff warning (3.10)–(3.11)
contents.reason: Supports the forward coordinate stencil and the warning that approximation and floating-point effects are distinct.

contents.name: §VI.3 Taylor error identity and Theorem 3.2 local Newton convergence proof
contents.reason: Independent local-Newton treatment read in full. Hairer assumes C^3 and an invertible Jacobian in a neighborhood; the local item proves the current contract's C^2 plus explicit Lipschitz-Jacobian version from its own suppliers.

contents.name: §VI.3 fixed inverse modification (3.12) and damped step modification (3.13)
contents.reason: Used to distinguish fixed-inverse and damped variants; no rate or accepted-step proof is attributed to the source.

contents.name: §VI.3 finite-difference Jacobian error and local Taylor argument
contents.reason: The source's scalar truncation expansion motivates the coordinatewise result; the vector norm bound and distinct component remainder points are proved locally.

contents.name: Chapter 4.5.2 vector linear model and Newton correction system
contents.reason: Independent textbook treatment supports solving the Jacobian linear system rather than forming a matrix inverse.

contents.name: Chapter 4.5.2 Newton system implementation and residual stopping parameters
contents.reason: Supports the finite iterative root-solving interface; the local algorithm makes its statuses and boundary order explicit.

contents.name: Chapter 4.5.2 statement that system Newton is quadratic under suitable circumstances
contents.reason: Context only: the page does not supply the proof or exact hypotheses used by the local theorem.

contents.name: Chapter 4.5.2 worked system iteration
contents.reason: Read as a comparison example; the assigned scalar, double-root, outside-neighborhood, and frozen-versus-updated examples are verified locally.
